title: Coulomb's Cabinet II: Algebra of Charge
summary: Route an exact charge into a vault by touching identical conductors, across mC, µC, nC and pC, without overloading the circuit.
subject: physics
learningOutcome: After winning, the student can add charges algebraically, deduce a hidden internal charge from a net charge, share charge between identical conductors, and convert between mC, µC, nC and pC.

levels.title: The Desync Circuit
levels.adds: Baseline: two terminals with mismatched charges, a blank sphere and a vault. Touch bodies together to route an exact charge into the vault.
hints: When two identical conductors touch, their combined charge is shared equally.
Add the two charges with their signs first, then halve.
A blank sphere is a handy way to split a charge in half.

levels.title: Prefix locks
levels.adds: New idea: the readouts mix mC and µC, and the vault door asks in a different prefix. A factor-of-1000 slip overloads the circuit.
hints: Convert everything to one unit before you compare: 1 mC = 1000 µC and 1 µC = 1000 nC.
The door's number is only comparable to the vault's reading once both are in the same prefix.
If an overload says you are off by a power of ten, a prefix was converted the wrong way.

levels.title: The sealed capsule
levels.adds: New idea: a cell hides a sealed capsule and the door only says "match it". Deduce its charge from the cell's net charge minus the listed parts.
hints: A cell's net charge is the algebraic sum of ALL its internal charges, the sealed capsule included.
Measure the cell with the electrometer, then subtract the listed charges from its net charge. Convert them to one prefix first.
Once you know the capsule's charge, plan the touches like in the earlier levels. A wrong seal tells you nothing.

levels.title: Down to picocoulombs
levels.adds: Harder: fine-scale charges and a picocoulomb target that needs a long chain of touches.
hints: Each touch with a blank sphere halves a charge: count how many halvings the target needs.
Plan the chain first so you never waste a touch.

misconceptions: Adding label numbers without converting prefixes
Thinking touching moves all the charge to the other body
